title: Northgate Care Protection Plans Purchase Conditions for a Sale Line
content:
**Clause.** A Northgate Care Protection Plans contract covers exactly one sale line, and a sale line may be covered by at most the plan's number of plans per sale line. A sale line already covered by a plan whose status is active may not be covered by another plan. A plan is bought only when it is purchased no later than the plan's purchase window in calendar days after the sale date of the covered product. Days are counted as calendar days, the sale date being day 0. The sale line must be in one of the plan's eligible merchandise classes, on one of its purchase channels, at a price between the plan's lowest and highest product price.

## The conditions, one by one

1. **One sale line.** The plan is bought for one sale line and covers that line alone.
2. **No active plan already on the line.** The company's plan records for that same sale line are the evidence: if a plan on that sale line has the status active, another plan may not be bought for it. What the member says about earlier plans does not replace the record.
3. **Purchase window.** The clock starts on the sale date shown on the company's record of the covered product's sale line, which is day 0. The plan purchase date may be no later than the day whose count equals the plan's purchase window; a purchase on that last day is within the window, and a purchase on any later day is not.
4. **Merchandise class.** The sale line's merchandise class is one of the classes the plan can be bought for.
5. **Purchase channel.** The sale line was sold on one of the purchase channels the plan can cover.
6. **Product price.** The price on the sale line lies between the plan's lowest and highest product price.

A plan is bought only when all six conditions hold.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates and window)

Take a hypothetical plan whose purchase window is 30 calendar days and a covered product sold on 2025-04-01 (day 0).

| Plan purchase date | Day count | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-04-01 | day 0 | Yes |
| 2025-04-30 | day 29 | Yes |
| 2025-05-01 | day 30 | Yes — the last day counts |
| 2025-05-02 | day 31 | No |

## Points of judgement

- **Which date starts the clock?** The sale date of the covered product's sale line, not the date the member asks about the plan and not the delivery date.
- **Which line is checked for an existing plan?** The very sale line the new plan would cover; an active plan on a different sale line, even on the same receipt, has no bearing on this condition.
- **Are calendar days the same as full 24-hour periods?** No; the count is of calendar days, the sale date itself being day 0.
